I'm working with Astro files and running the linter with the rule that suggests converting regular imports to type-only imports.

*   When linting an Astro file with the useImportType rule enabled, a component import must NOT be flagged for conversion to a type-only import if that component is referenced as a JSX element in the Astro file's template section (the markup area after the closing frontmatter delimiter).

*   JSX component usage in the Astro template section (e.g., using an imported identifier as a rendered element tag) must be recognized as a value-position reference, preventing the useImportType rule from incorrectly suggesting the import be converted to a type-only import.

*   When the useImportType rule is applied to an Astro file where a component import is used both in a type context in the frontmatter (such as via typeof in a generic type argument) and as a JSX component in the template, linting must complete with no diagnostics and no fixes applied.

*   Linting an Astro file with experimentalFullSupportEnabled and the useImportType rule must produce the output 'No fixes applied' when all component imports are correctly used as rendered elements in the template section.


**CRITICAL:** Do not modify any files in the `tests/` directory.
The verification system will apply test patches automatically.
Your task is to implement the feature in source files only.

**Biome** is a performant toolchain for web projects, it aims to provide developer tools to maintain the health of said projects. **Biome is a [fast formatter](./benchmark#formatting)** for _JavaScript_, _TypeScript_, _JSX_, _JSON_, _CSS_ and _GraphQL_ that scores **[97% compatibility with _Prettier_](https://console.algora.io/challenges/prettier)**. **Biome is a [performant linter](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/tree/main/benchmark#linting)** for _JavaScript_, _TypeScript_, _JSX_, _JSON_, _CSS_, and _GraphQL_ that features **[more than 450 rules](https://biomejs.dev/linter/javascript/rules/)** from ESLint, typescript-eslint, and [other sources](https://github.com/biomejs/biome/discussions/3). It **outputs detailed and contextualized diagnostics** that help you to improve your code and become a better programmer! **Biome** is designed from the start to be used [interactively within an editor](https://biomejs.dev/guides/editors/first-party-extensions/). ## Summary

I implemented support for recognizing JSX component usage in an Astro file's template section as a value-position reference for the `useImportType` rule.

### Root cause

Astro files without `experimentalFullSupportEnabled` are parsed with only their **frontmatter** treated as JavaScript; the template section (markup after the closing `---` fence) was never parsed. So a component imported and used *only* as a JSX element in the template looked like an unused import — and if that same import was *also* used in a type position in the frontmatter (e.g. `typeof Component` in a generic type argument), the rule saw a type-only usage and incorrectly suggested converting it to `import type`.

Biome already had the machinery to track template component names (`EmbeddedValueReferences::visit_html_root`, used for Vue/Svelte and for Astro under full support), but it was never invoked on the non-full-support Astro path.

### Change

In `crates/biome_service/src/workspace/server.rs`:

- Added a helper `track_astro_template_value_references` that re-parses the whole Astro file content with the Astro HTML parser (`HtmlParserOptions::from(&HtmlFileSource::astro())` — frontmatter fence + single text expressions), then walks the resulting `HtmlRoot` to record component element names as value references.
- Wired it into both document-parsing paths (`insert_document` and `change_file`) as an `else if path.extension() == Some("astro")` branch, after the existing Vue/Svelte/full-support HTML branch. This only fires for Astro files that aren't already handled as HTML (i.e., non-full-support), so it doesn't disturb the full-support path.

### Verification

- Built `biome_service` and the `biome` CLI; drove real `.astro` files through `biome lint --only=useImportType`:
  - `typeof Component` in frontmatter generic + `<Component />` in template → **No fixes applied** ✓
  - member component `<A.B />` + `typeof A` → clean ✓
  - import used only as a type with **no** template usage → still correctly flagged (no regression) ✓
  - full-support path → still **No fixes applied** ✓
- All 30 existing `handle_astro_files` tests pass, plus the Vue/Svelte suites (70 tests), confirming no regressions.

No files under `tests/` were modified.
